key_findings.finding: Fog is the single highest-impact PS1 horror aesthetic technique — both atmospheric AND a performance-saving measure (Silent Hill benchmark)
key_findings.implementation: Apply FogExp2 at density 0.0012-0.0015 with cold cyan color (0x003344) to all 4 scenes; currently 3 of 4 scenes have fog bugs (wrong density, wrong color, or missing FogExp2)

key_findings.finding: CRT emulation requires 5 composited effects (barrel distortion, chromatic aberration with per-channel RGB offset, scanlines with time animation, noise grain, vignette) — CSS-only approach can reach at most ~40/100 fidelity
key_findings.implementation: Three.js EffectComposer + custom ShaderPass: barrel distortion on UV → sample R at +1 offset, B at -1 offset for chromatic aberration → multiply by time-animated scanline texture → composite noise texture with per-frame randomization → blend vignette at edges → output. Retain CSS crt.css as fallback.

key_findings.finding: Low-resolution texture pipeline is structural: 64x64 textures + point filtering (no interpolation) + vertex jitter (0.3-0.8 unit random displacement) create authentic PS1 look
key_findings.implementation: Enforce 64x64 or 128x128 texture cap; set Three.js texture magFilter/minFilter to NearestFilter; add custom vertex shader with random position displacement

key_findings.finding: Loneliness is the core emotional mechanic of PS1 horror — achieved through minimal sound design (sparse drones, isolated footsteps, no music), empty environments, and limited visibility
key_findings.implementation: One low-frequency drone per scene, player footstep audio with reverb, no background music, wind/water at 20% volume

key_findings.finding: Liminal spaces derive power from being transitional (hallways, pools, underpasses), empty-but-not-abandoned, with fog obscuring boundaries — Dreamcore adds cryptic text overlays on top of liminal base
key_findings.implementation: Add occasional cryptic UI text fragments fading in/out at random screen positions; add subtle human-trace artifacts to scenes (lit window, abandoned object); procedural fog density variation

key_findings.finding: Render resolution should be intentionally degraded: disable anti-aliasing, set pixel ratio to 0.5-1.0, no MSAA
Fixed camera angles in key moments create helplessness and tension; optional player-toggleable CRT effects increase immersion buy-in
key_findings.implementation: Trigger-zone based camera lock (3-5 seconds); [T] keybind cycles CRT modes (off/light/full)

crt_effects.consensus: STRONG — WebGL shader required, CSS insufficient

loneliness_isolation.consensus: MODERATE — design philosophy, harder to measure

fixed_camera.consensus: WEAK — single source, period-accurate but niche

consensus_findings: Fog is the defining PS1 horror technique — all design and technical sources agree
CRT requires multi-effect compositing, not single-effect overlay
Low-res textures + point filtering are structural, not cosmetic
Cold color palette is non-negotiable for horror atmosphere

contradictions.source_b: AOgl-MRi26A — terrain tree placement broken with PSX shader
contradictions.resolution: Source B is correct; source A later acknowledges this. For Three.js: manually construct low-poly terrain geometry, do not rely on automated systems.
CSS can reach ~40/100 fidelity; WebGL shader required for 80+. Current approach is acceptable as fallback but must be supplemented with WebGL CRT pass.

unique_insights.insight: Psychic automatism — procedural elements create more authentic liminal feeling than hand-designed scenes
unique_insights.application: Add random fog density variation, random particle drift, random dreamcore text fragment timing

unique_insights.insight: Fixed camera angles create more tension than first-person for certain horror moments
unique_insights.application: Implement trigger-zone camera locks for key liminal reveals

unique_insights.insight: CRT toggle as player-facing option solves readability complaints without removing aesthetic
unique_insights.application: Add [T] keybind cycling through CRT modes
